5.0.s.en: (1) The end of the love of money

5.0.0.en: Your miseries that shall come upon you: eternal torment.

5.0.2.en: Motheaten: the moth is a small insect that eats clothes.

5.0.3.en: The Apostle James calls the rich who rely on their money to weep and howl, because their miseries are coming. They were occupied with gathering earthly treasures and loved perishable things more than God. He describes what will happen to them: their riches will be dissipated and their garments will be corrupted and eaten by moths. Even the precious metals will rust and lose their shine, and all this will be a witness against them and a cause of their torment in the fire of hell, because the poor man was in need and they did not give to him, and even in the last days of their life, instead of being occupied with the heavenly treasure, they were occupied with gathering perishable earthly treasures, so they lost everything on earth and in heaven, and in the end themselves.

5.1.0.en: Kept back by fraud: you reduced the wages of those who work in them, that is, you gave them less than their due.

5.1.1.en: The love of money leads to selfishness and cruelty, and here is the wage of the laborer who sowed and reaped the fields of the rich, which they have unjustly withheld from him; and the cry of those wronged people has been heard by the mighty God, expressed as “the Lord of sabaoth”, who is able to do all things and defends the wronged.

5.2.0.en: The rich live in luxury and ease, as if they were fattening their hearts, which have become hardened by sin, like fatted calves for the day of slaughter, so that the fattened body becomes food for worms, as the Holy Bible says, “But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth” (1 Tim 5:6).

5.3.0.en: They have also condemned the innocent and weak and imprisoned him, and the poor man they have killed with hunger, and he cannot resist them.

5.3.1.en: The Apostle James gives us his practical teachings, that the treasures of the world perish and vanish, so lay up for yourself treasure in heaven, as the Lord Christ said in (Mt 6:19). So if you meet a poor man, or an opportunity to do good, do it, and trust that it is a precious opportunity God has given you, so do not waste it, for it will not return again.

5.4.0.en: The precious fruit of the earth: the fruits of the harvest, which signify the eternal reward.

5.4.1.en: The early rain: which waters the winter crops in the autumn season, and signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in the sacrament of Baptism and His encouragement of believers at the beginning of their spiritual striving.

5.4.2.en: The latter rain: which waters the winter crops at the beginning of spring, a short time before the harvest ripens, and signifies the help of the Holy Spirit to believers during their striving and until the end of their life.

5.4.3.en: He calls the poor and the wronged to stand firm in the faith, to be patient and to take a lesson from the farmer, who sows and plows and waits patiently for the crop until it drinks the early rain of autumn and the latter rain of spring, and to wait for the salvation of the Lord and His coming, when He will reward them in eternity, for whoever looks to Christ in His coming finds his sufferings easy.

5.5.1.en: He commands that the poor and wronged man not murmur against the rich man nor judge him or seek vengeance on him, because the rich man is wretched and held in the hand of Satan, and lest the poor man be condemned for his murmuring. And let him remember that Christ will come as Judge to give each one according to his works (Mt 7:1).

5.6.0.en: The Apostle calls them to be patient and to wait for the salvation of the Lord, because He does not let them be tempted above what they are able to bear, and he put before them the prophets’ patient endurance of suffering so that they may follow their example.

5.7.0.en: He gave them an example of patience, which is “Job”, and how God rewarded him, because he endured the death of his children, sickness, poverty and mockery, so God praised him and then gave him twice as much as he had had.

5.8.0.en: The Gospel forbids swearing, for how can we swear by something we do not own?! Everything we own belongs to God and we are stewards over it. If your speech is always truthful, people will trust you, because the upright tongue speaks one word, without interpretation or twisting. The true Christian, who is always truthful in his speech, does not need to swear for people to believe him, as the Lord Christ said, “Swear not at all” (Mt 5:34). On the other hand, it is not fitting for us to swear by the name of God or by anything else, because Satan exploits the word of an oath in an hour of anger, as happened when Herod killed John the Baptist (Mt 14:7).

5.9.s.en: (3) Prayer and the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick

5.9.0.en: He calls them, if they meet with afflictions and trials, to lift up their hearts to God, who feels for them and suffered for them on the Cross, so He supports them and they do not feel weary because of their great sense of God’s consolations. And if God gives them gifts and delivers them from trials, let them express their joy in a spiritual way and not in evil like the people of the world. The expression of joy is by praise and psalm-singing, and therefore the Church has arranged hymns of praise that are said every day, in addition to the hymns of the various occasions.

5.10.0.en: Elders: priests, which is the correct translation in the Greek language and also in the versions approved by the Orthodox and Catholic Churches, but in the Protestant versions we have at hand the word was translated “elders” because the Protestants do not believe in the sacrament of the priesthood.

5.10.1.en: The Apostle James affirms that the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick was established and practiced in the apostolic age, and he directs the believers’ attention to calling the priests, that is, the clergy, to visit the house where there is a sick person, to pray over him the prayer of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick and to anoint him with the oil upon which the Holy Spirit has descended through prayer.

5.11.0.en: He stresses the importance of faith in the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick so that the sick person may be healed, whether his own faith or the faith of the priests or the faith of those around him, and he adds to this the necessity of repentance and confession of sin before the priests present during this sacrament, so that the sick receive forgiveness of their sins in addition to healing from their bodily illnesses.

5.12.0.en: The sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick was practiced with a large number of people present in the house. Seven priests would come, or at least more than one priest in the case of severe illnesses, and in this gathering he calls those present to confess their sins before the priests present, so that the first group is the people and the second group is the priests. Of course it is unreasonable that he means the priests confessing before the people, or the people confessing to one another leaving aside the priests who are present.

5.12.1.en: He also asks those present to pray with one heart for the sick person so that he may be healed, and that this should be their constant conduct, praying for one another; and here he singles out especially the priests who lead the prayer during this sacrament.

5.12.2.en: He stresses the value of prayer that comes from a pure heart before God, for it is able to heal diseases. Here appears the importance of intercession, which the early Church held to in the days of the Apostles. The “righteous man” is of course the saint, and the intercession of the saints is able to do many things and God rejoices in it, because whoever holds to it shows his humility and faith, and likewise his love for the saints.

5.13.0.en: The Apostle confirms his words with the story of the prophet Elijah (1 Kgs 17:1), who was a man of human nature like us, exposed to sufferings and afflictions, and prayed in faith that it might not rain, and the rain stopped for three years and a half, in order to call the people to repentance and the worship of God and to leave the worship of idols; and when many of them returned to God, he prayed a second time and the rain fell, and the earth sprouted and bore fruit and the famine ended. Thus appear the importance of the prayers of the saints and God’s concern to answer them.

5.13.1.en: Prayer is a power that moves the whole world and draws down the mercies of God, especially if it comes from a repentant, pure heart in need of God, in supplication and faith. So do not delay, but hasten to God in all your needs and press Him however great your request, trusting in His love and mercy.

5.14.s.en: (4) Visiting those who have gone astray

5.14.0.en: He urges the believers to care for one another, so that if one of them departs from the faith or goes astray into grave sins, they should hasten to care for him and call him to repentance with humility and love, and so save him from eternal destruction, so that his sins are not exposed before the Church, but he returns a living member in her.

5.14.1.en: Here appears the importance of service. God is the Savior, but He rejoices in our spiritual service to one another and blesses it and completes it. St. Gregory affirmed this meaning with his words, “If the one who saves a person from bodily death, though he will die some day, deserves a reward, how much more does he deserve who saves a soul from eternal death.”

5.14.2.en: These verses confirm the possibility of a believer’s perishing and answer the Protestant innovations that say the opposite, and the Apostle Paul confirms the same meaning with his words, “Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him” (Heb 10:38), and he also says, “Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling” (Phil 2:12). Then he proves it with real evidence when he says, “For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ” (Phil 3:18).

5.14.3.en: Care for the salvation of those around you, especially your household, relatives and friends, and if they do not accept your direct word, offer them love and care and pray for them.
